Hi Helena — thanks, this is clear and helps us scope the architecture. High-level proposal: 

- EU primary: customer VPC (preferred) with private endpoints to Redwood Private runtime nodes deployed in EU-only subnets. All logs and backups written to an EU-resident storage account you control.
- APAC standby: a separate Redwood Private deployment in APAC (air-gapped from EU) configured for passive async replication. Replication encrypted in transit and at-rest with different KMS keys scoped to APAC.
- Control plane: we will offer a customer-controlled control plane option (VPC peering or private link) so audit events can be forwarded to your SIEM in-region.
- Networking: recommend native cloud interconnect (ExpressRoute/Interconnect/ExpressLink) or a managed SD-WAN tunnel. Avoid cross-region VPC peering that causes automatic routing of customer traffic to APAC.
- Failover model: manual, orchestrated failover with documented checklist. Target RTO 30–60 mins for control-plane-driven cutover; RPO depends on replication cadence — default async snapshot every 5 mins gives RPO ~5–10 mins.

Questions for your infra team:
1) Do you require the APAC replica to be encrypted with a vendor KMS or must it be customer-managed in-region?
2) Any contractual requirements for routing (BGP vs static) or approved providers for physical cross-connects?
3) Do you want Redwood to host a passive DNS health-check endpoint to initiate, or will that live on your side?

I'll loop in our infra and security folks to produce a network diagram and a detailed RTO/RPO matrix.

Thanks,

Marissa / team — summary of proposed technical design and notes for the customer: 

1) Topology (attached: nb_network_diagram_v3.png)- EU Primary: Redwood runtime nodes deployed in FR/DE/NL subnets inside the customer's VPC via PrivateLink (no public ingress). Data plane endpoints are regional and connect to customer-managed EU storage buckets for backups/logs.- APAC Standby: separate Redwood Private deployment in the selected APAC region (SG/SYD). Standby nodes are not part of the EU routing tables and have a strict one-way replication channel from EU -> APAC.

2) Replication and keys- Replication: asynchronous block-level replication using encrypted tunnels over the customer's private interconnect (recommended). We'll ship a replication agent in the EU deployment that pushes snapshots to APAC.
- KMS: customer-managed keys required. We recommend distinct KMS keys per-region with key policies that prevent export of plaintext keys. We'll store key IDs in our regional control-plane connectors; plaintext keys never leave customer KMS. (see kms_region_mapping.csv)

3) Networking and failover mechanics- Connectivity: recommended: Direct Connect / Interconnect / ExpressRoute. Fallback: IPsec tunnels with redundant carriers.
- DNS and traffic cutover: put health-check TTLs at 60s. Failover is triggered manually by customer (or Redwood ops with documented authorization). Upon authorization: update DNS to point to APAC endpoints, start warming caches, and bring standby into read/write mode.
- BGP: optional for fully automated routed failover; caution: BGP-based active-active can violate residency constraints if misconfigured. We recommend active-passive to stay compliant.

4) RTO / RPO estimates (baseline)
- Async replication every 5 mins -> expected RPO 5–10 mins (depends on outstanding writebuffers).- Cold-start standby (no warm caches) -> RTO 45–90 mins.
- Warm standby (pre-initialized runtime nodes, DB warmed) -> RTO 20–35 mins.

5) Auditability and controls- All failover actions logged to EU-resident audit log. Post-DR, produce a signed runbook entry including who authorized, timestamp, reason, and whether data was accessed in APAC.

6) Tests and cadence- Quarterly tabletop, biannual full failover DR test (with roll-forward plan). We will provide a test script and acceptance criteria.

7) Edge cases / compliance notes- China and certain APAC jurisdictions may require separate intake. This design excludes China; if needed, a separate deployment is required.
